name: The Emptied Font

detectability.signature: A shimmering meniscus of compressed starlight surrounding a volume that returns no mass, energy, or vacuum-energy readings

proximity: Instruments register falling vacuum energy as the boundary nears
Navigation instruments give contradictory readings across the meniscus
contact: Light entering the boundary redshifts to invisibility within meters
Probe telemetry stretches, slows, and stops
prolonged_exposure: Shields drain as ambient vacuum energy is consumed around the hull
Crew report color draining from both vision and recent memory

phenomena: A ring of compressed starlight crowning the boundary
Visible distortion of starfield beyond the rim
Navigation instruments giving contradictory readings near surge maxima
hazards: Power system overload and total battery depletion
known_incidents: The automated refinery Cup and Crumb strayed across the boundary during a surge; her recovery crew found the vessel intact, cold, and utterly batteryless
Surge watchers observed the pocket swallow a comet whole in 2401, leaving not even debris
description: The Emptied Font is a three-thousand-kilometer bowl of near-nothing, crowned by a ring of starlight bent steeply around its rim like water gathering at a basin's lip. Within the boundary sensors find almost no vacuum energy at all, a depletion so complete that light itself thins and dies a few meters past the meniscus. The effect reads less like a hole and more like a volume that has been drunk.

On a rough fifty-two-hour rhythm the pocket surges, its appetite deepening and its rim brightening without warning or discernible pattern. Anything skimming the boundary during a surge is drained: batteries, shields, momentum, warmth. Comets have crossed and left no crumbs.

Stellar archaeologists estimate the Font has been emptying its surroundings for seven hundred million years, and the system's paucity of small bodies may be entirely its doing. It was named by a supply clerk rather than a scientist, after the first probe came home powered down to its rivets. Physicists value it as the sharpest known gradient in vacuum energy anywhere surveyed.

Shipping lanes bend wide around the surge envelope, which forecasters remap each cycle and never quite trust. Research platforms observe from standoff distances measured in planetary radii. The standing question, whether the Font will someday fill or instead finish emptying everything, is why the watchers stay.
